title: Intra-topic latency as an automated behavioral marker of treatment response in autism spectrum disorder.
summary: Across 210 child-social-partner dyads at four sites, the treatment group showed greater pre/post reduction in child latency than the matched treatment-as-usual group (change-score difference p<0.001, d=0.43); latency also correlated with ADOS-2 calibrated severity score. Full-text Methods and Results use repeated-measures mixed models with clinical covariates and examine site effects. This was not randomized; intervention and control representation differed by site, and 46.4% of dyads had different partners across visits. Authors call for validation in controlled trials and broader populations.
ai_technology: A two-layer feed-forward DNN classifies speech/non-speech from MFCCs, while ASR and lexical-coherence segmentation identify conversation topics; the resulting intra-topic response latency is the studied behavioral measure.
organization: Department of Psychiatry, Weill Cornell Medicine, New York, NY, USA

source_review.scope: The primary full text documents an automated signal-processing/ML measure of intra-topic conversational latency and a specific four-site clinical finding in 210 children with ASD. In the treatment group, child latency declined from 2.94 to 2.69 seconds while the treatment-as-usual group increased from 2.63 to 3.05 seconds; the adjusted treatment contrast remained significant. The version of record was published 2022-02-28. Exact DOI/title checks found no active or archived match. The observational, nonrandomized design and site imbalance limit causal interpretation; the result is a candidate response measure, not proof of treatment efficacy.
